editorial:
The Animal Kingdom is a 1932 film adapted from Philip Barry's play of the same name, which opened on Broadway on January 12, 1932. Its US copyright status is undetermined.

If the film was registered in 1932, a renewal would have been due in 1959 or 1960 and would appear in the Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes for those years. I have not searched either volume, so I cannot say whether a renewal exists. I have also not found the film's original registration date. The Copyright Office online catalog (1978 and later) is only a secondary check.

The open risk is the source play. It is a separate copyright, and I have not searched its registration or renewal. If the play was renewed and the film is a derivative work, Stewart v. Abend reasoning could let the play's owner restrict reuse, so clear that before commercial reuse. The easy-to-find Internet Archive copy is colorized. Colorization is added material, so use an uncolorized print if you want only the free layer.
faq: Was the copyright on the 1932 film The Animal Kingdom renewed?

I don't know. A renewal of a 1932 registration would be in the 1959 or 1960 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes. I have not searched them. I also did not find the original registration date.
Can I use the colorized Internet Archive copy in my project?

Use caution. Colorization is added material and can carry its own claim, even if the underlying black-and-white film is free. Use a plain scan of the original print. Also check the registration and renewal of Philip Barry's 1932 source play, which I have not searched.
